newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine blue-chips close down after Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine blue-chips close down after Brazil.

text.p: Argentine stocks bounced off lows but closed down Friday in a session which traders said was depressed by falls on Wall Street and in Sao Paulo.
The blue-chip MerVal index MERV crash through to the psychological 800-point barrier, but toned down losses to close at 802.11, 1.62 percent down from Thursday.
"The market was influenced by the big falls in Brazil and New York," said Humberto Lopez, of Wainbuch y Compania.
"But the Argentine market is holding up. In the past, the bourse would have matched the fall in Brazil," he added.
The Bovespa stock index was 4.66 percent lower with brokers citing factors including sales by domestic equity funds. On Wall Street, the Dow Jones ended down 1.62 percent.
"The market is going through a correction, which at certain prices is tempting some players to rebuy positions they sold out of at last week's prices," said Lopez.
Turnover was $27.4 million, down from $30.2 million Thursday and $36.7 million last Friday.
"The lower volume shows that the market is going through a phase of price adjustment, which could go on until the middle of next week," a trader said.
A total of 52 stocks closed down, 10 up and 13 unchanged.
But traders said the market could climb again in August, when preliminary company results should lure buyers.
